factors.name: growthFundingCapacity
factors.basis: Nebius closed $5.75 billion aggregate principal of convertible senior notes on August 24, 2026 and stated that proceeds are intended for data-center construction, AI-cloud development, footprint expansion and key components including GPUs.

risks: The financing adds substantial convertible debt and therefore future interest, refinancing and potential dilution/overhang considerations belong in Alpha underwriting.
The company exchanged $800 million aggregate principal of older convertible notes for approximately 15.8 million Class A shares, creating an explicit equity-supply/dilution consideration.
unknowns: This source does not quantify project-level returns, deployment timing, utilization, incremental margins or eventual conversion dilution.

factors.name: capitalExecution
factors.basis: The financing is a completed transaction rather than a financing intention: $3.45 billion principal of 0.50% notes due 2030 plus $2.30 billion principal of 4.50% notes due 2034, providing source-addressed capital for the stated buildout plan.

risks: Capital availability does not prove that capacity can be built on time or monetized at attractive returns.
Convertible structure can transfer part of execution risk into future dilution or balance-sheet burden.
unknowns: Net proceeds after fees, exact allocation by project and realized return on deployed capital remain outside this source.

sources.origin: U.S. SEC EDGAR / Nebius Group Form 6-K Exhibit 99.1
facts: Nebius closed $5.75 billion aggregate original principal amount of convertible senior notes: $3.45 billion of 0.50% notes due 2030 and $2.30 billion of 4.50% notes due 2034.

Nebius stated that net proceeds are intended to finance business growth including data-center construction/build-out, full-stack AI-cloud development, footprint expansion and procurement of key components including GPUs.
Nebius separately exchanged $400 million principal of 2029 notes and $400 million principal of 2031 notes for approximately 15.8 million Class A ordinary shares.

result: Materially different SEC-filed capital-structure evidence packaged for Alpha. It improves source-addressed funding-capacity and dilution/risk inputs without creating Alpha numeric underwriting.
